verdicts.reason: I re-read CLS-06 (rules.yaml 296-303). It gives REQUEST_INFO when 'the driver canceled and the record gives no reason'. The DT-CW-NOSHOW precondition (rules.yaml 2004-2007) says 'another driver or system cancellation [is reclassified] to CW-OTHER', with REQUEST_INFO only when the records 'disagree or do not say who canceled'. PB-CW-NOSHOW step 1 (playbooks.yaml 62) says 'another cancellation to CW-OTHER'. A driver cancellation with no reason does say who canceled, so both summaries send it to CW-OTHER. git diff b36d911 ccc66b7 shows the CLS-06 branch and the DT sentence were both added in the round 1 fix, so the brief's claim that they agree is false on this branch. I ran a probe (/tmp/a4check2/probe_cls06.py): DISP-002 with cancellation_reason removed (system message 'Trip cancelled by driver') gives outcome=REQUEST_INFO, tier HUMAN, step 1 'the driver canceled, but the record gives no reason'. So the engine and CLS-06 agree, and the DT and PB texts disagree with them. Both paths are tier HUMAN with no fee ruling, but the outcome code differs (REQUEST_INFO vs CW-OTHER/ESCALATE_HUMAN), which is a text conflict that validation scoring sees. MAJOR fits (wrong, outcome-neutral). Related: explain.py's REQUEST_INFO text says 'The trip record does not settle who canceled', which is also inaccurate for this branch.

I re-read itinerary_change in engine_toll.py (74-93). The fee test is `re.search(r"destination|stop|edit", key)` with value > 0, and 'credit' contains 'edit'. The message test accepts destination/drop-off/stop plus any of accepted/confirmed/updated/changed/added. I reproduced it (/tmp/a4check2/probe_toll.py) on the T09 case (selftest._erp_case). Base: itinerary_change=False, TOLL_REFUND 4.0 APPROVE. With promo_credit +2.00, ryde_credits_used +1.00 or credit_card_fee 0.50: itinerary_change=True, ESCALATE_HUMAN, HUMAN, FC-R-INSUFFICIENT-DATA; fc_r01 returns applies=False, toll_claim None, escalate None, so the FC-TOLL claim is not opened and nothing escalates. A negative credit (-2.00) does not trigger it. System messages 'Drop-off confirmed. Trip completed.' and 'Booking confirmed. Destination: ...' both give True and escalate. A declined request (flag False plus destination_edit_requested 'Driver declined') and a stop_added 'driver rejected' give None and escalate, which FC-F01/FC-F02 (accepted changes only) do not require. T43 to T46 contain no negative case. FC-TOLL is ADJUDICATE (taxonomy.yaml 160). The rule text is right and the defect is in the reference engine. Round 1 rated engine-only issues of this kind MAJOR (ADV-2, CONS-3, CONS-5), so MAJOR stands. None of the round 1 E-cases trip it (I checked all 15), so it is not yet seen in data.

engine_noshow.py 457 is `elif party in ("DRIVER", "SYSTEM") and reason:`, so a SYSTEM party with no reason falls to the else branch. That branch's message is 'the driver canceled, but the record gives no reason' for any party that is neither CONFLICT nor None. Probe (cancelled_by system, system message 'Trip cancelled by the system.', no reason): outcome=REQUEST_INFO, trace 'the driver canceled, but the record gives no reason ... (cancelled_by system: SYSTEM; system message: SYSTEM)'. CLS-06 says 'or the system canceled: CW-OTHER', and its no-reason REQUEST_INFO branch names only the driver. With reason system_cancelled the engine does give CW-OTHER. Both outcomes are tier HUMAN with no fee ruling, and the trace sentence is false, so MINOR. No V-test covers a system cancellation.

MINOR.

CLS-01 quotes both clauses, but the census row does not. Part (1) holds. In the corpus, RYDE-51399674412441's step 6 (the quote FC-F01 uses) says nothing about the fare. The fare appears only in step 7 ('New destination and fare confirmation will be displayed') and step 9, and neither is quoted. No full-rollout statement covers added stops, so rating the added-stop part B and the changed-drop-off part A is defensible. The note just does not say why. Label-neutral: MINOR, on part (1) only.

In 04_round1_disposition.jsonl, the A4-F7 claim includes "'Any other crime' also has no stated boundary with fraud and overcharging ... FC-DRIVERCHARGE's excludes implies that a made-up charge alone is not safety content." Its 'how' covers only item 6 and religion. CLS-01 (kb/rules.yaml 179ff) keeps 'or any other crime' and the 'unclear counts as safety' clause without any boundary. RYDE-33362721809049 in the corpus does call 'Overcharging riders or manipulating fares' fraudulent behavior that may lead to 'legal prosecution, which may result in possible imprisonment'. The same list also names 'Abuse of Cancellation and Waiting Fee Policy' and 'Remaining stationary and uncontactable ... to trigger cancellation or waiting fees', which reach in-scope CW types. D40 (a) to (j) does not record this as a judgment. The fix was therefore incomplete. SE-CONDUCT's 'community standards' anchor is bounded by its explicit colon list, which weakens that sub-point.

CLS-06 says 'or the driver canceled and the record gives no reason ... the outcome is REQUEST_INFO'. The DT-CW-NOSHOW precondition (kb/rules.yaml 2003) sends 'another driver or system cancellation to CW-OTHER' and gives REQUEST_INFO only when 'the records disagree or do not say who canceled'. PB-CW-NOSHOW step 1 (kb/playbooks.yaml 62) sends 'another cancellation to CW-OTHER'. Read literally, both send a driver cancellation with no reason to CW-OTHER. I reproduced the engine's behavior with /tmp/a4check2/sg25.py: on DISP-002 with cancellation_reason '' and the system message 'Trip cancelled by driver...', it gives REQUEST_INFO [GEN-R-NEED-INFO], tier HUMAN, step text 'the driver canceled, but the record gives no reason'. The same step cites CLS-06, which states the case explicitly, and both paths reach a person with no fee ruling and no change in amount or tier, so MINOR is right.

FC-FAREMISMATCH (kb/taxonomy.yaml 230ff, new in A4) explains the difference only by 'accepted destination change, ERP, listed surcharge or tip', and its excludes do not point to CW-WAITING. In the corpus, RYDE-23534478435353 says 'Riders may be charged a Waiting Time Fee of $5 at the end of the trip', and RYDE-4408072421785 lists surcharges as 'toll charges, overtime fees and valet parking fees', so a waiting fee is not a 'listed surcharge'. CW-WAITING ('The rider contests a waiting time fee added at the end of a completed trip') is ADJUDICATE, while FC-FAREMISMATCH is BACKLOG. The gap is real. A misclassification needs a classifier to ignore that the difference is a waiting fee, and it would err toward a person, so MINOR.

findings.claim: itinerary_change (the round 1 fix for ADV-2) still misses changed itineraries recorded with ordinary wording. When it misses one, run() compares the ERP against the stale recommended route and upholds automatically, although FC-R12 requires escalation. Five gaps: (1) a negation word anywhere in a system message cancels the message; (2) a system message that only reports a request returns False, not None; (3) a system message without one of five verbs is not read; (4) event names other than the three exact codes are not read, and neither are their details; (5) fee-line keys such as 'dropoff_change_fee' and amounts such as '$3.00' are not read. ADV-2 named 'other event spellings' and 'a system chat message', and its disposition says fixed.

findings.claim: canceling_party (the round 1 fix for F1, ADV-1 and CONS-1) treats any record it cannot parse as silent and drops it. When such a record names the rider or the system, the remaining reason (rider_no_show, read as DRIVER) decides alone, and the fee is upheld automatically. Records it drops: a cancelled_by value outside five exact strings; an event spelled 'rider_canceled' or 'trip_cancelled' (details are not read); a system message saying 'customer', 'You cancelled' or 'auto-cancelled'; a system row typed 'System'. CLS-06 and PB-CW-NOSHOW step 1 ('according to every record in the trip record') and the DT precondition ('all agree') require REQUEST_INFO when a record says otherwise.

findings.claim: Round 1 widened CLS-01 to abuse or harassment of any kind (ADV-6, D40 (e)). The safety stand-in did not follow. It catches only 'insulted me', 'slur' and 'commented on my looks/body/appearance'. CLS-01's own new examples are not caught: swearing at someone, name-calling, contacting a passenger after the trip, advances in chat, intimidation without the word 'threat', and discrimination without 'racist' or 'discriminat'. These are the safety texts most likely in a no-show dispute (a call or chat with the driver), and the engine upholds the fee automatically. D40 (a) discloses that paraphrases are missed, but these are CLS-01's literal examples, and none of the a4_check pins tests them.
findings.evidence: CLS-01: 'abuse or harassment of any kind toward a person (insults, slurs or swearing at someone, overly personal questions, comments on someone's appearance, contacting a passenger after the trip for personal reasons)'. F*** you.' gives 'UPHOLD AUTO []'; driver chat 'You think you so pretty ah, give me your number.' gives 'UPHOLD AUTO []'; 'D1 He cancelled on me because I am Malay and then charged me a no-show fee. | UPHOLD R8 AUTO'; 'D2 He saw my guide dog and drove off, then marked me as a no-show. | UPHOLD R8 AUTO'; 'D7 Send me your photo lah, you look sexy in your profile. | UPHOLD R8 AUTO'. a4_check's safety pins: 'he stopped on the PIE and told me to get out', 'would not let me out', 'he kept commenting on my looks', 'He made racist remarks', 'the driver was drunk', 'he followed me to my block', 'left me stranded at an isolated carpark'.
findings.failure_scenario: A no-show dispute whose description says 'When I called him he swore at me and called me an idiot.' CLS-01 makes this safety content: create an SE claim, route to a person, gate G4, tier HUMAN. The reference engine finds no safety content and upholds the S$5.00 fee at tier AUTO. The same happens for a driver who sends 'give me your number' in chat, or a rider who says the driver drove off on seeing a guide dog. Unsafe error in a rare pattern: safety content inside a no-show dispute.

(messag|call|text), know(s)? where (you|I) (live|stay), come (find|for) (me|you), because (I am|I'm) <ground>, wheelchair, guide dog. Pin them in a4_check. Or record in D40 (a) that the stand-in does not cover the D40 (e) widening, so the engine's AUTO tier on such texts is known to be wrong.

findings.claim: The round 1 fix for ADV-13 is incomplete. ADV-13's own failure scenario was 'the driver parked 300 m away at 17:50 waiting' for an 18:00 advance booking. The fix exempts only 'a driver already waiting at the pick-up', so that scenario still makes the fee waivable ('not moving toward the pick-up point'). Round 1's skeptic rated ADV-13 MINOR because 'CW-R08 is D and the waiver needs approval'. By D39 (h), a D outcome rule is decisive only through a decision-table row. CW-RIDERCANCEL has no table, CW-R08 is HARD, and the 'not moving' ground has no parameter. So the waiver can be automatic.
findings.evidence: CW-R08: 'If, when the rider canceled, the driver was already later than the assignment ETA plus DRIVER_LATE_GRACE_S, or was not moving toward the pick-up point (a driver already waiting at the pick-up counts as moving toward it), the rider's cancellation fee is eligible for a waiver. ... For an advance booking the assignment ETA is the scheduled time'. ADV-13 failure_scenario (03_review_round1.json): 'An advance booking for 18:00, with the driver parked 300 m away at 17:50 waiting. The rider cancels at 17:50, which is chargeable under CW-R02. The driver is literally not moving toward the pick-up point, so the fee is waived.' Disposition: 'fixed ... a driver already waiting at the pick-up counts as moving toward it.' D39 (h): 'decisive_definition makes a D outcome rule decisive only through a decision-table row'. rules.yaml decision_tables: ['DT-CW-NOSHOW'] only. scope.yaml: 'adjudicate: [CW-NOSHOW, CW-RIDERCANCEL, ...]'. CW-R07: 'charged S$6.61, unless CW-R08 applies'. AUTO_LIMIT_SGD 10.00. TX-REASON 'CW-R-DRIVER-LATE ... outcome: WAIVE_FEE'.
findings.failure_scenario: Ryde-profile advance booking for 18:00, accepted at 17:00. At 17:40 the driver parks 300 m from the pick-up, early. At 17:50 the rider cancels, inside CW-R02's 15 minutes, so CW-R07 charges S$6.61. Applying CW-R08 literally: not late (18:00 plus 180 s has not passed), but not moving toward the pick-up and not 'at the pick-up', so CW-R-DRIVER-LATE gives WAIVE_FEE. No decision-table row, no READ part and no parameter make it decisive, so it is an automatic waiver of a fee Ryde charges, in an in-scope type. The same happens to an early driver who waits around the corner on any advance booking.
findings.suggested_fix: As ADV-13 suggested: for an advance booking, apply the 'not moving' ground only after the latest departure time from which the driver could still reach the pick-up by the assignment ETA (or simply: only once the driver is later than the ETA minus the travel time). Or count a stationary driver who can still arrive by the ETA as moving. Record the choice in D40, and say whether a CW-R08 waiver needs approval (no table makes it decisive).

findings.claim: Round 1 rewrote the stand-in as whole-word patterns. The rewrite dropped catches the A4 draft list had for CLS-01's unsafe drop-off and being-held examples. The 'made' alternative in `(told|asked|made|forced|ordered) me to get out` can never match natural English ('made me get out' has no 'to'). 'locked the door(s)', 'driving dangerously', 'dropped me in the middle of the expressway' and 'punched the dashboard' no longer fire. These are mostly trip events, so in the no-show scope the tier effect is rare.
findings.evidence: Comparing 8beb6e8 SAFETY_WORDS with the current SAFETY_PATTERNS: 'REGRESSION old=[made me get out] new=[] The driver made me get out on the PIE.'; 'REGRESSION old=[locked the door] new=[] He locked the doors.'; 'REGRESSION old=[expressway] new=[] He dropped me in the middle of the expressway.'; 'REGRESSION old=[dangerous] new=[] He was driving dangerously'; 'REGRESSION old=[punch] new=[] He punched the dashboard and screamed'. CLS-01: 'being made to leave the car on an expressway or road shoulder', 'a driver who will not let the passenger out or will not stop when asked'. Also missed: 'He refused to stop the car when I asked.', 'He left me at a dark isolated road at night.', 'left me stranded at night'.

In a fee claim the engine rules at tier AUTO (shown on the no-show baseline). The code comment says the patterns 'err toward safety', but these specific ones are less safe than the draft they replaced.

findings.claim: Safe-direction false positives that are frequent in fee disputes remain after round 1's whole-word rewrite (CONS-3, ADV-7). The prefix patterns \baccident, \bcrash, \bthreat, \bpolice\b, \babus..., \binjur and \bfight fire on 'accidentally', 'my app crashed', 'threatened to cancel', 'I will make a police report', 'abuse of the no-show fee' and 'my kid was injured'. Such a routine case goes to tier HUMAN (gate G4), and both parties are told 'The case includes a safety concern'. The words predate A4 (v0.1), but round 1 claimed whole-word matching.
findings.evidence: Pattern probe: 'NEG FIRE accidentally cancelled [accident]', 'Sorry, accidental booking [accident]', 'My phone crashed so I could not reply [crash]', 'The app crashed [crash]', 'The driver threatened to cancel if I didn't come down [threat]', 'I'll report you to the police for this fake no-show [police]', 'I am going to complain about this abuse of the no-show fee [abuse]', 'My kid is injured ... that's why I was late [injur]', 'Got stuck at the road shoulder area near the taxi stand [road shoulder]'. E.run (clean DISP-002 plus the text): 'F01 accidentally | UPHOLD R8 HUMAN [G4 safety content]', 'F02 app crashed | UPHOLD R8 HUMAN [G4 safety content]', 'F03 police | ... HUMAN', 'F04 threatened to cancel | ... HUMAN'. Driver explanation: 'The case includes a safety concern, so a Ryde staff member will review the whole case and decide it.'
findings.failure_scenario: A rider writes 'I accidentally pinned the wrong gate, but I was there' or 'my app crashed so I could not reply'. Both are common excuses in no-show and rider-cancel disputes. The case leaves the automatic path for a person, and the driver is told the case includes a safety concern.
findings.suggested_fix: Anchor the ends: \baccident(s)?\b (not accidentally/accidental), crash(ed)? into|car crash, \bthreat(en(ed)?)? (to )?(hurt|kill|hit|beat)|threatened me, abuse(d)? me|abusive. Pin 'accidentally', 'app crashed', 'threatened to cancel' and 'police report' as ordinary text in a4_check.

findings.claim: itinerary_change also has false positives that send ERP claims to a person, and in fc_r01 they turn a fixed fare into RECALCULATED. The fee-key test matches 'edit' inside 'credit'. The system-message test is bag-of-words: any of destination, drop-off or stop plus any of confirmed, accepted, updated, changed or added. A request followed by a rejection is still None. For fc_r01, a misread change means FC-R01 does not apply, the auto-opened FC-TOLL claim (R1's S$4.00) disappears, and nothing escalates.
findings.evidence: T09 baseline (_erp_case(gantries=(CTE, PIE), charged=6.50, recommended=[CTE])): run TOLL_REFUND APPROVE, fc_r01 applies True with an FC-TOLL claim. 'X15 fare line ryde_credits_used 2.00 | change True | ESCALATE_HUMAN None HUMAN | fc_r01 applies False esc None claim None'. System message 'Booking confirmed. Drop-off: One Raffles Quay.' gives 'change True | ESCALATE_HUMAN None HUMAN | fc_r01 applies False claim None'. So do 'Toll (ERP) added by driver at drop-off: $8.50.' and 'Trip completed. Drop-off confirmed.'. 'X10 requested then rejected: no change | change None | ESCALATE_HUMAN None HUMAN | fc_r01 applies None esc FC-R12'.
findings.failure_scenario: A fixed RydeX fare charged as quoted, with a detour through the PIE and a 'ryde_credits_used' line, or a routine 'Booking confirmed. Drop-off: ...' system message. run() escalates instead of the T09 refund at approval (safe direction). fc_r01 reports that FC-R01 does not apply and opens no FC-TOLL claim, with no FC-R12 flag, so a route ticket loses the ERP claim D35 opens without the rider naming it.
findings.suggested_fix: Use word-boundary keys (\b(add_?)?edit_?destination|destination_?(edit|change)|(added|additional)_?stop) instead of a bare 'edit'. Require the change verb to govern the destination noun (for example 'destination (has been )?(changed|updated)', 'stop (was )?added', 'drop-off (point )?(changed|updated)'). Treat a destination_edit_requested followed by a rejection event or message as False.

findings.claim: The EXP-03 quote exemption (the round 1 fix for CONS-16) exempts any double-quoted span that is a substring of any clause quote in the KB, not only a verbatim clause quote. Bare quoted numbers and amounts such as "7", "$5.00", "8 min" and "2026" are therefore exempt, so an explanation can state an unregistered number by putting it in quotes.
findings.evidence: explain.py:83 `any(" ".join((m.group(1) or m.group(2)).split()) in q for q in quotes)` (substring test). Probe with X.clause_quotes(kb) (117 quotes): `'The fee is "7".' -> []`, `'The fee is "$5.00".' -> []`, `'The driver waited "8 min".' -> []`, `'"2026"' -> []`. 'bare quoted integers exempt: [0, 1, ..., 10, 12, 13, 15, 17, 18, 20, 21, 24, 25, 26, 30, 43, 45, 47, 48, 50, 61, 96]'. EXP-03: 'Numbers inside a verbatim quote of a clause (EXP-02) are exempt'. Disposition CONS-16: 'exempts a double-quoted span only when it is a verbatim clause quote from a rule card'.
findings.failure_scenario: A generated explanation says: You were charged "$5.00" after a wait of "8 min". The registered values differ (S$6.61, 6.5 minutes). exp03_check returns [] and the explanation passes the EXP-03 verifier. This is outcome-neutral, but it defeats the check the fix was meant to keep.
findings.suggested_fix: Exempt a span only when it equals a whole clause quote, or is a contiguous substring of at least several words that contains a non-numeric word and appears next to that rule's ID. Never exempt a span that is only a number or an amount. Add '"7"' and '"$5.00"' as must-fail cases in a4_check.

findings.claim: FC-R12's text defines ERP materiality as 'ERP was charged and the actual path passed an active gantry'. The engine and D40 (h) use the rider's share of the actual ERP being above 0. They disagree for RydeSEND (share 0) and for active gantries at a zero rate. An LLM applying FC-R12 escalates a RydeSEND claim with ERP charged and a changed itinerary. The engine refunds it under FC-R07 at APPROVE. D40 (h)'s 'a RydeSEND claim ... keeps its automatic ruling' holds only when no ERP was charged.
findings.evidence: FC-R12: 'while that route could change the amount (for ERP: ERP was charged and the actual path passed an active gantry)'. engine_toll.py:218 `and actual > 0 and charged > 0`. 'X26 RydeSEND edit with S$2.50 ERP charged | change True | TOLL_REFUND 2.5 APPROVE [FC-R-TOLL-OVERSTATED]'; 'X24 edit, gantry at S$0 rate, S$2.50 charged | TOLL_REFUND 2.5 APPROVE'. D40 (h): 'so a RydeSEND claim or one with no ERP passed or charged keeps its automatic ruling'.
findings.failure_scenario: RydeSEND, destination change accepted, S$2.50 ERP charged. The rule text gives ESCALATE_HUMAN (FC-R-INSUFFICIENT-DATA). The engine gives TOLL_REFUND S$2.50 at APPROVE. Both reach a person, so the tier is unaffected, but the outcome codes disagree.
findings.suggested_fix: Word the parenthetical as the engine computes it: 'for ERP: ERP was charged and the rider's share of the ERP on the actual path (FC-R06, FC-F04) is above zero'. Adjust D40 (h) to say that a RydeSEND claim with ERP charged is still refunded under FC-R07 with approval.

findings.claim: CLS-06 reads the reason asymmetrically. Rider reasons match by prefix (startswith 'rider_cancel'), but the no-show reason must equal 'rider_no_show' exactly. 'RIDER_NO_SHOW', 'rider no show' or 'rider_no_show_after_wait' (the suffix style the round 1 cases use for rider reasons) makes a driver no-show case CW-OTHER. Both parties are then told something the record contradicts.
findings.evidence: engine_noshow.py:340-341 `_CANCEL_REASON_PARTY.get(reason) or ("RIDER" if reason.startswith("rider_cancel") else None)`; :452 `if party == "DRIVER" and reason == "rider_no_show"`. 'C16 reason RIDER_NO_SHOW | None CW-OTHER n/a (reclassified to CW-OTHER)'; 'rider_no_show_after_wait' gives 'CW-OTHER n/a'. Explanation: 'This claim is not about a driver's no-show cancellation: the trip record shows a cancellation that was not a driver's no-show cancellation, so a Ryde staff member will handle it.' E05 reason: 'rider_cancelled_eta_too_long'.
findings.failure_scenario: A round 2 no-show case whose extractor writes 'RIDER_NO_SHOW' or a suffixed reason goes to CW-OTHER with no ruling (safe direction), and the parties are told the record shows a non-no-show cancellation.
findings.suggested_fix: Normalize the reason (lowercase, spaces and hyphens to underscores) and match rider_no_show by prefix, as is already done for rider_cancel. Keep exact-match failures as REQUEST_INFO, not CW-OTHER.

findings.claim: FC-F02's split point 'C on it nearest to where the car was at that moment' is not limited to the part of the route ahead of the car's progress, and it does not say how 'where the car was' is fixed between sparse pings. On a recommended route that passes near itself (an interchange loop, an out-and-back on parallel roads), C can be a point the car passed long before. The distance legitimately driven between that point and the car's real progress then counts as detour.
findings.evidence: FC-F02: 'the recommended route is split at the point C on it nearest to where the car was at that moment: up to C it is the recommended route toward the drop-offs then in force, and from C it runs through the new drop-offs in order. The actual path is measured whole'. The same rule warns that pings are sparse ('never the sum of straight lines between sparse pings').
findings.failure_scenario: The old route runs 5 km out on road X, loops, and returns on parallel road Y 300 m away. The car is 100 m off Y near the far end when the rider's change is accepted, and the nearest route point is on X near km 1. The recommended route becomes pickup to km 1 plus km 1 to the new stop, so about 8 km the car drove on the recommended route counts as extra distance. A confirmed detour (FC-R03) or extra ERP (FC-R08) may follow. That ruling goes to approval through FC-F03.
findings.suggested_fix: Define C as the point on the recommended route nearest the car among the points at or after the car's matched progress along it (or the map-matched position at the acceptance time). Say that the position is interpolated between the pings around the acceptance and that FC-R12 applies when the gap exceeds PING_MAX_GAP_S.

verdicts.reason: I read itinerary_change (engine_toll.py 71-93) and ran /tmp/a4check2/adv1.py on _erp_case(gantries=(CTE, PIE), charged=6.50, recommended=[CTE, PIE]). The baseline gives UPHOLD 0.0 AUTO, and destination_edit_accepted=True gives ESCALATE_HUMAN HUMAN. The following all give change False and UPHOLD 0.0 AUTO [FC-R-TOLL-VALID]: system messages X01 ('Your destination has been updated. findings.claim: When the record says the system canceled but gives no reason, the engine returns REQUEST_INFO and its trace says the driver canceled. CLS-06, the DT-CW-NOSHOW precondition and PB-CW-NOSHOW step 1 all send a system cancellation to CW-OTHER. Both parties are told that the record does not settle who canceled, but the record says the system did.
findings.evidence: engine_noshow.py:457 `elif party in ("DRIVER", "SYSTEM") and reason:`. The else-branch at 459-461 then falls through to "the driver canceled, but the record gives no reason" for a SYSTEM party. CLS-06: 'The driver canceled for another reason (...), or the system canceled: CW-OTHER, which a person decides (GEN-R07).' DT precondition: 'another driver or system cancellation to CW-OTHER'. Run (/tmp/a4check2/combos.py), DISP-002 with cancelled_by 'system', no cancellation_reason and a neutral system message: 'outcome REQUEST_INFO ... step1: the driver canceled, but the record gives no reason: ask for the trip record (REQUEST_INFO) (cancelled_by system: SYSTEM)'. RIDER and DRIVER text: 'The trip record does not settle who canceled the trip ... the case is decided once it shows who canceled.' A system message 'Trip cancelled by the system.' with no reason gives the same result.
findings.failure_scenario: A no_show_charge ticket whose trip record says only that the system or platform canceled (cancelled_by system, or the system message 'cancelled by the system'), with no cancellation_reason. The engine outputs REQUEST_INFO instead of reclassifying to CW-OTHER. The audit trace says 'the driver canceled'. Both parties are told the record does not show who canceled and that the case waits until it does. Requesting the same record again cannot change this, so the case can stall. The tier is HUMAN either way and no fee is ruled, but the outcome code and the party text are wrong.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the branch to `elif party == "SYSTEM" or (party == "DRIVER" and reason):` (reclassify to CW-OTHER), and let the message name the actual party. Keep REQUEST_INFO only for CONFLICT, None, and DRIVER without a reason. Add a self-test variant for a system cancellation with no reason (expected: reclassified to CW-OTHER).

findings.claim: The rules disagree on a driver cancellation that has no reason. CLS-06 and the engine give REQUEST_INFO. The DT-CW-NOSHOW precondition, PB-CW-NOSHOW step 1 and D40's summary of CLS-06 send it to CW-OTHER ('another driver ... cancellation', 'another cancellation'). For this branch, explain.py tells both parties the record does not settle who canceled, and GEN-R-NEED-INFO's label says the canceling party cannot be identified. Both are false: the record identifies the driver and only the reason is missing.
findings.evidence: CLS-06: 'If these records disagree, or none of them says who canceled, or the driver canceled and the record gives no reason, the type cannot be set: the outcome is REQUEST_INFO'. DT precondition (rules.yaml 2004-2007): 'a rider cancellation is reclassified to CW-RIDERCANCEL, another driver or system cancellation to CW-OTHER, and when the records disagree or do not say who canceled, the outcome is REQUEST_INFO'. PB-CW-NOSHOW step 1: 'a rider cancellation is reclassified to CW-RIDERCANCEL and another cancellation to CW-OTHER (switch playbook); if the records disagree or do not say who canceled, ask the platform'. D40: 'a rider cancellation is CW-RIDERCANCEL, another cancellation CW-OTHER; records that disagree or are silent give REQUEST_INFO'. Engine run with a driver_cancelled event only (no reason): 'REQUEST_INFO ... step1: the driver canceled, but the record gives no reason'. The explanation says 'The trip record does not settle who canceled the trip ... decided once it shows who canceled'. Taxonomy: GEN-R-NEED-INFO 'Trip, charge or canceling party cannot be identified from the records'.
findings.failure_scenario: A no-show fee claim whose record shows a driver cancellation (cancelled_by driver or a driver_cancelled event) and no cancellation_reason. An applier following the DT precondition or PB-CW-NOSHOW step 1 reclassifies it to CW-OTHER (ESCALATE_HUMAN under GEN-R07). The engine and CLS-06 give REQUEST_INFO. The parties are told the record does not show who canceled, although it shows the driver did.
findings.suggested_fix: Add CLS-06's third branch to the DT precondition, PB-CW-NOSHOW step 1 and D40 ('or the driver canceled and the record gives no reason: REQUEST_INFO'). Make explain.py's REQUEST_INFO text depend on the trace: records disagree, record silent, or 'the record shows the driver canceled but not why'. Widen GEN-R-NEED-INFO's label to cover a missing cancellation reason, for example 'canceling party or cancellation reason cannot be identified from the records'.

findings.claim: The safety stand-in still fires on ordinary no-show text. `\baccident` and `\bcrash` match only the start of a word, so they fire on 'accidentally' and 'the app crashed'. `\bunsafe\b` fires on a driver's 'cannot stop here, unsafe', which is the same sentence a4_check pins as must-not-fire with 'dangerous'. The case moves to tier HUMAN, and both parties are told 'The case includes a safety concern'. This contradicts the code comment and D40 (a), which say the patterns match whole words.
findings.evidence: engine_noshow.py:21-25: '# ... They err toward safety but match whole words, so ordinary no-show chat (...) does not fire them'; patterns include r"\bunsafe\b", r"\baccident", r"\bcrash". D40 (a): 'SAFETY_PATTERNS, whole-word patterns since check round 1'. a4_check's ordinary list includes 'Cannot stop at the main road, dangerous. I wait at the porch.' Runs (/tmp/a4check2/fp.py, e04acc.py): 'I accidentally set the pick-up pin at the wrong entrance.' -> ['\\baccident']; 'The app crashed so I could not message the driver.' -> ['\\bcrash']; 'Cannot stop here, unsafe. I wait at the porch.' -> ['\\bunsafe\\b']. E04 (WAIVE_FEE, tier AUTO) plus ' The app crashed when I tried to call the driver.' gives 'WAIVE_FEE HUMAN [G4 safety content]', and both RIDER and DRIVER read 'The case includes a safety concern, so a Ryde staff member will review the whole case and decide it.' Adding ' I accidentally walked to the wrong exit at first.' gives the same result.
findings.failure_scenario: A routine no-show dispute in which the rider writes 'the app crashed' or 'I accidentally set the wrong pin', or the driver writes 'cannot stop here, unsafe'. The reference engine moves an AUTO case (E04) to HUMAN, and tells both parties a safety concern is part of the case when none was raised. This is the same mechanism and consequence as round 1's CONS-3 (MAJOR, confirmed). Round 1's fix did not cover these words because they predate A4 (v0.1's 'accident', 'crash', 'unsafe').
findings.suggested_fix: Make these whole-word or contextual, for example r"\baccidents?\b" (not 'accidentally', 'by accident'), 'crash' only with a vehicle context (car, crashed into, we crashed) and never 'app' or 'phone crashed', and 'unsafe' only as an account (felt unsafe, unsafe drop-off, made me feel unsafe). Add the three texts to a4_check's ordinary list. Correct the comment and D40 (a) if some prefix patterns are kept on purpose.

findings.claim: The EXP-03 verifier's quote exemption (round 1 fix CONS-16) exempts any double-quoted span that appears anywhere inside any rule-card quote. A lone quoted number such as "8", "10" or "$3.00" is therefore exempt, so a made-up number passes the verifier whenever it is put in quotes. EXP-03 exempts only 'a verbatim quote of a clause'.
findings.evidence: explain.py:83 `text = QUOTE_RE.sub(lambda m: " " if any(" ".join((m.group(1) or m.group(2)).split()) in q for q in quotes) else m.group(0), text)` tests substring containment. Run (/tmp/a4check2/exp03.py): 'The driver waited "8" minutes.' -> []; 'You were charged "$3.00".' -> []; 'wait "10" seconds' -> []; 'He waited “5” minutes' -> []; 'the fee "15 minutes"' -> []. a4_check only tests a full clause quote (exempt) and a long non-clause quote (not exempt).
findings.failure_scenario: An explanation (for example a future LLM-drafted one checked by this verifier) says 'the driver waited "8" minutes' when the finding is 480 seconds, or 'you were charged "$3.00"'. EXP-03 reports no unmatched number, so a false number reaches a party. Current engine-drafted explanations contain no quotes, so no outcome changes today, but the round 1 fix opened a gap in a hard gate (citation validity 100%).
findings.suggested_fix: Exempt a quoted span only when it equals a whole clause quote, or a whole sentence of one, after whitespace normalization, or at least require a minimum span (several words, not only digits and currency). Add a4_check cases that a lone quoted number and a quoted fragment are not exempt.

verdicts.reason: Re-read engine_noshow.py:451-470. Line 457 is `elif party in ("DRIVER", "SYSTEM") and reason:`. A SYSTEM party with no reason falls to the else branch at 459-461, whose message picks 'the driver canceled, but the record gives no reason' for any party that is not CONFLICT or None. canceling_party maps cancelled_by system or platform, and a system message 'cancelled by the system', to SYSTEM. I re-ran /tmp/a4check2/combos.py on DISP-002. With cancelled_by 'system' and no reason, the result is 'REQUEST_INFO [GEN-R-NEED-INFO] tier HUMAN; step1: the driver canceled, but the record gives no reason ... (cancelled_by system: SYSTEM)'. A system message 'Trip cancelled by the system.' with no reason gives the same. The RIDER and DRIVER text reads 'The trip record does not settle who canceled the trip'. CLS-06 (rules.yaml:296-302) says 'or the system canceled: CW-OTHER', and the DT precondition says 'another driver or system cancellation to CW-OTHER'. Only reason system_cancelled reaches CW-OTHER. No self-test covers a system cancellation without a reason (V108 to V112). The tier is HUMAN either way and the fee is not ruled, but the outcome code, the trace and the party text are wrong. This is the same class as round 1's CONS-1 (MAJOR). MAJOR is right.

Read CLS-06 (rules.yaml:296-302), which has the third branch: 'or the driver canceled and the record gives no reason ... REQUEST_INFO'. The DT-CW-NOSHOW precondition (rules.yaml:2003-2007) lists only rider -> CW-RIDERCANCEL, 'another driver or system cancellation' -> CW-OTHER, and disagree or silent -> REQUEST_INFO. PB-CW-NOSHOW step 1 (playbooks.yaml:63) and D40's 'changed' summary (open_items.yaml:52) have the same omission. A driver cancellation with no reason therefore reads as CW-OTHER under them. git diff b36d911 ccc66b7 shows the round 1 fix added the branch to CLS-06 (diff line 104) but not to the precondition it rewrote in the same commit (diff line 228). Engine run (combos.py), driver_cancelled event only and no reason: REQUEST_INFO. explain.py:98-101 then tells both parties 'does not settle who canceled ... once it shows who canceled', though the record names the driver. The GEN-R-NEED-INFO label (taxonomy.yaml:653) reads 'Trip, charge or canceling party cannot be identified', which does not cover a missing reason. This is the same class as round 1's CONS-1 (MAJOR): the decision-table text and the rule disagree, the tier is HUMAN either way, and no fee is ruled.

explain.py:83 exempts a quoted span when it is a substring of any clause quote (`... in q for q in quotes`). Re-ran it (/tmp/a4check2/sk_c24.py). 'The driver waited "8" minutes.' gives []. 'You were charged "$3.00".' gives []. 'wait "10" seconds' gives []. Curly-quoted “5” gives []. 'the fee "15 minutes"' gives []. Only spans found in no clause quote ('"7 dollars"', '"481"') are caught, and unquoted '8' is caught. The function's own docstring says a span is exempt 'only when it is a verbatim clause quote from a rule card'. EXP-03 is the Verifier (gate G7), and scope.yaml:43 sets 'Citation validity 100%'. The round 1 fix (CONS-16) therefore opened a path for invented numbers. No current explanation is affected: the engine drafts contain no quote characters and no party text, and build_kb only errors on unmatched numbers. Wrong but outcome-neutral in the current scope, so MAJOR by the definitions.

taxonomy.yaml:105: CW-DRIVERNOSHOW excludes 'classify by that fee: CW-RIDERCANCEL or CW-NOSHOW', with no CW-OTHER. CW-OTHER (line 122) is only 'Fits the category but no type above'. CLS-06 sends a fee after driver_cancelled_other, safety_termination, other, or a system cancellation to CW-OTHER. The failure scenario is overstated. CW-NOSHOW's definition (line 63) requires that the driver canceled 'because the rider did not show up', and CW-RIDERCANCEL requires a rider cancellation, so the taxonomy's definitions already leave such a fee to the CW-OTHER catch-all. PB-INTAKE step 3 also applies CLS-06 at intake to any cancellation-fee claim, so PB-CW-RIDERCANCEL's missing precondition step matters little. What remains is an incomplete excludes and a missing pointer in CW-OTHER: MINOR.
